newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish tourism board to restore shamrock as logo.
newsitem.headline: Irish tourism board to restore shamrock as logo.

text.p: Ireland's Tourist Board, Bord Failte, has been ordered to restore the shamrock as the symbol of Irish tourism, dropping a new logo designed a year ago at a cost 100,000 Irish pounds.
Tourism minister Jim McDaid has ordered a traditional symbol of Ireland, a shamrock, be reinstated.
"It is something I feel very strongly about. I am personally committed to the shamrock as our traditional symbol and I don't think we should dispense with it," McDaid said.
The new logo which replaced the shamrock last November met with a mixed response and McDaid was critical of the decision to spend so much money on the new design.
"In my opinion there was absolutely no need to get rid of the shamrock. I don't think the 100,000 punts was well spent.
